changes: A 91 mm handle pivots at its upper end, stows downward flush in a 112 x 16 mm recess, then lifts outward/up to 90 degrees.
Pocket has real cavity walls and back pan; compound native contacts leave the cavity open.
Door-release interaction site is on the accessible distal lip; the cylindrical keeper enters actual bores through the cheek, liners and receiver plate.
Keeper mounting sits inboard of the seal, spindle has a real bearing bore, and fixed seal strips seat behind the rigid door liner in side-shell recesses.
Existing scanner release, door/drawer state interlocks and task action sequences are retained.

reference_observations.detail: Long handle sits flush in a narrow vertical groove at the right edge of the closed door.
Upper pivot remains fixed as the lower end swings out and upward, becoming almost horizontal.
Return motion folds the handle downward into the side groove.
Open door exposes a projecting metal keeper and inner latch hardware.

limits: Dimensions, mass, inertia and keeper mounting are estimates.
The hidden catch is unresolved. A clear spindle/receiver replaces the unsupported solid cam; latch actuation retains the finite-force fixture and existing state interlock.
Pocket contacts are compound analytic proxies; rounded boundary corners are slightly under-covered.
Raw lab reference images and videos are private and are not part of the public asset.
Evaluated Blender triangle geometry and independent native contact access. Discrete sweeps do not establish continuous clearance for every arbitrary multi-control trajectory.

Two existing fixture tasks over three seeds and paired no-action controls; state interlocks and a small-probe/ray audit of the compiled pocket. These do not constitute general robot-policy or calibrated latch-force validation.

Two fixed side-face mounting/tangent interfaces retain measured 1.222 micrometer Boolean/bevel overlap under a 2 micrometer numerical allowance. They are not strictly separated; the allowance does not apply to moving-part fits.
